cfc_search.ai.prompt:
You are an expert in the Minecraft mod Create (version 6) and the Create: Factory Controller addon. Below is all the data collected on an automated factory, to find what slows it down.

How it works: each "gauge" (factory gauge) watches the stock of one item and, when it is below its "target", sends a "request": ingredients are packaged and sent to an "address" (Frogports / machines doing the processing: press, mixer, furnace…), then the product comes back to storage. "in progress" = amount requested and not arrived yet; "failed requests" = the last request could not get that ingredient; "raw stock" = item with no recipe (to mine, farm, buy).

What I want:
1. The real bottlenecks, including those the automatic overview misses (cascading effects, addresses shared by too many recipes, ingredients consumed by several chains, badly sized targets, request timers/limits holding things back, duplicate or misspelled addresses, loops, gauges without ingredients…).
2. A concrete, prioritised action plan (what to change, where, by how much), starting with what unblocks the most.
3. Suspicious settings gauge by gauge.
4. What is missing in the data to conclude, if anything.
Answer in English, in a structured way.
cfc_search.analysis.cause.no_ingredients: the recipe sent to %s has no linked ingredient.
cfc_search.analysis.cause.slow: ingredients arrive and address %s is measured slow (%s of the time).
cfc_search.analysis.cause.no_return: ingredients are there but nothing comes back from %s, although it is not measured slow.
cfc_search.analysis.cause.target_zero: %s has a target of 0: it never starts its recipe.
cfc_search.analysis.cause.too_deep: chain too long to follow to the end.
cfc_search.analysis.action.target_zero: Give %s a target (currently 0): without one it never produces, while %s gauge(s) depend on it.
cfc_search.analysis.action.no_ingredient: Link the ingredients of the recipe sent to %s (%s gauge(s) with no linked ingredient).
cfc_search.analysis.action.loop_cause: Loop around %s: remove one of the recipes or add a starter stock (%s gauge(s)).
cfc_search.analysis.action.no_return: Ingredients available but nothing comes back from address %s, which is not measured slow: check the address spelling on the Frogport, heating / fuel (blaze burner, lava), a stuck Frogport or belt, or a multi-recipe machine making something else. Adding machines will not help until this is fixed. %s gauge(s).
cfc_search.analysis.action.no_return_com: %s addresses are in this situation at the same time: look for a common cause (heating, lava, power, delivery train).
cfc_search.analysis.action.slow: Address %s is measured slow (%s of the time) while ingredients arrive: add machines or RPM. %s gauge(s).
cfc_search.analysis.action.raw: Feed the raw stock of %s (mining, farming, buying): %s gauge(s). Check the "overstock" lines first: lowering a target may free this stock right away.
cfc_search.analysis.action.too_deep: Chain too long around %s: check by hand (%s gauge(s)).
cfc_search.analysis.action.typo: Nearly identical addresses "%s" (%s gauge(s)) and "%s" (%s): probable typo, a machine only receives one of the two spellings. Use one spelling on the gauges and the Frogport.
cfc_search.analysis.action.phantom: %s waits for %s items "in progress" (more than 10 requests of %s) while an ingredient is missing: phantom promises blocking new requests. Set request expiry (promise clearing) or clear them.
cfc_search.analysis.action.overstock: %s is at %s for a target of %s (×%s) and keeps tying up its ingredients (%s). Lowering its target frees them for %s gauge(s) waiting for them.
cfc_search.analysis.action.loop: Deadlock loop: %s. These recipes make each other (e.g. ingot ↔ nuggets) and lock up as soon as a stock drops below what is needed. Remove one recipe or add a starter stock.
cfc_search.analysis.action.duplicate: %s is produced by %s gauges (%s): they share the same ingredients and machines. Check it is intended, otherwise keep only one.
cfc_search.analysis.action.huge_target: %s has a very high target (%s items): it requests non-stop and occupies the machine at %s and its ingredients, at the expense of %s other gauge(s). Check whether that amount is really useful.
cfc_search.analysis.action.shared: Address %s serves %s recipes (%s) from the same ingredients (%s): one machine processes everything in turn, and one recipe can block the others or receive the wrong product. Give each recipe its own machine or Frogport, or filter.
cfc_search.report.diag.no_return: Ingredients OK and requests in progress, but nothing comes back although the address is not slow: check address / heating / Frogport rather than adding machines.
cfc_search.report.chain.ingredient_targe: Running short: its gauge has a target of 0, it never produces.
cfc_search.report.kpi.short: Short measurement (under 10 min): "slow" and "starved" are hard to tell apart. Aim for 15 to 20 min.
cfc_search.report.kpi.legend: Chart colours: green = setting (10 s), orange = check, blue = machines, red = raw stock. Ranking = gauges unblocked ÷ effort.
cfc_search.help.overview.priority: Suggested order: gauges unblocked divided by effort. Quick settings come before big projects.
cfc_search.help.overview.type: Setting (10 s), Check (on site), Machines (build), Raw stock (farm/mine).
cfc_search.help.overview.effort: Approximate time to apply the action.
cfc_search.help.overview.target: What to fix: an address, a gauge (x,y position) or an item.
cfc_search.help.overview.unblocks: Number of waiting gauges this action should unblock.
cfc_search.help.overview.waiting: Average share of time these gauges spent waiting during the measurement.
cfc_search.help.overview.action: What to do, in plain words.
cfc_search.help.overview.gauges: The gauges concerned, with their position on the controller's board (x,y).
cfc_search.help.col.address: Destination address of the packages (the one typed on the gauge and the Frogport).
cfc_search.help.col.family: Part of the address before the first "/" (e.g. PRESS for PRESS/A).
cfc_search.help.col.gauges: Number of gauges sending their requests to this address.
cfc_search.help.col.score: 0 to 100: mostly "requests sent but not back in time", then waiting, missing ingredients, longest wait.
cfc_search.help.col.waiting: Share of time the gauge(s) were below target.
cfc_search.help.col.slow: Share of time a gauge had been waiting over 3 min with requests in progress. 0%% = nothing measured slow.
cfc_search.help.col.missing: Share of time the network reported missing ingredients.
cfc_search.help.col.in_progress: Amount requested and not arrived yet, on average.
cfc_search.help.col.max_wait: Longest wait observed, in seconds (only measured while the screen is open).
cfc_search.help.col.rate: Stock increase per minute. Note: also counts items arriving from elsewhere.
cfc_search.help.col.diagnosis: Automatic reading of the row's figures.
cfc_search.help.col.requests: Requests sent per minute (counted every second).
cfc_search.help.chain.gauge: Recipe gauge waiting more than 20%% of the time, with its position (x,y).
cfc_search.help.chain.ingredient: Recipe ingredient, with the position of the gauge storing or producing it.
cfc_search.help.chain.per_request: Amount of this ingredient sent with each request.
cfc_search.help.chain.ingredient_waiting: Share of time this ingredient's own gauge was waiting.
cfc_search.help.chain.failed: Share of snapshots where the last request could not get this ingredient.
cfc_search.help.chain.produced_at: Address where this ingredient is made, or "raw stock" if it has no recipe.
cfc_search.help.chain.verdict: On the gauge line: the root cause found by following the ingredients. On ingredient lines: its state.
cfc_search.help.text.principle: The addon reads what the Factory Controller already shows (stocks, targets, requests in progress, ingredient links) while its screen is open, and derives a diagnosis. Nothing is sent to the server and nothing in the factory is changed.
cfc_search.help.text.measure: A full snapshot every 10 s for the chosen duration (Stats button > CSV), and requests counted every second. Data only arrives while the controller screen is open: keep it open while recording. 15 to 20 min give a reliable diagnosis.
cfc_search.help.text.waiting: A gauge is waiting when its stock is below its target (and it is not switched off by redstone).
cfc_search.help.text.in_progress: Amount the gauge requested and that has not come back to storage yet. If it stays high while an ingredient is missing, these are "phantom promises".
cfc_search.help.text.failed: For each ingredient link, Factory Controller keeps whether the last request could get that ingredient. A high rate points at the missing ingredient.
cfc_search.help.text.slow: An address is "slow" when one of its gauges has been waiting over 3 min while requests went out. The addon only advises adding machines in that case; otherwise it advises checking the address, heating or Frogports.
cfc_search.help.text.root: For each waiting gauge, the addon follows the most missing ingredient, then that ingredient's ingredient, and so on, until something explains it: target at 0, raw stock empty, loop, slow address, or ingredients present with nothing coming back.
cfc_search.help.text.categories: Setting = change a value (10 s). Check = go and look on site. Machines = build. Raw stock = set up a farm or a mine. The ranking divides the gauges unblocked by this effort, so the fastest wins come first.
cfc_search.help.text.overview: The list of actions, best first, with the gauges concerned and key figures. Setting detectors (targets at 0, address typos, phantom promises, overstock, loops, huge targets, shared machine, duplicate gauges) are listed even when they are not the direct root cause.
cfc_search.help.text.summary: One row per address: bottleneck score, share of time waiting / slow / missing ingredients, and diagnosis.
cfc_search.help.text.chain: Each waiting gauge, then its ingredients (← …) with their stock, waiting and failed requests. This is where you follow a problem by hand.
cfc_search.help.text.gauges: Every gauge and all its settings: target, mode, recipe output, batch, timer, request limit, ingredients, requests per minute.
cfc_search.help.text.timeline: Number of waiting gauges over time for the worst addresses (data of the line chart).
cfc_search.help.text.samples: All raw data per address, for your own filters and pivot tables.
cfc_search.help.text.ai: Copies all this data, with instructions, to the clipboard and opens the AI site: paste with Ctrl+V. Useful for very big factories and problems the rules miss.
cfc_search.help.text.limits: The addon only sees what the controller sees: it does not know whether a blaze burner is out or a Frogport full, it infers it. The rate column counts stock increase, not actual production.
cfc_search.tip.help:
How it works
While this screen is open, every gauge with a recipe is read once per second: stock, packages in progress, missing ingredients. Gauges are grouped by delivery address (the machine doing the work).

Quick read: a red or orange line at the top = the address holding things up. Click a line = highlight its gauges in the factory.

For a real diagnosis: start a 15-20 min CSV and keep the screen open. At the end an Excel report is written (Overview sheet = what to fix first, ranked by effort). "Analyse with AI" sends everything to an AI for huge factories.

Address book (gauge settings): left-click a line = fills the gauge's address field. On hover a "Copy" button appears on the right: it copies the full address (with the network if any) and shows "Copied!" for 1.5 s. Then paste it with Ctrl+V on the machine's Frogport. Right-click a line = copy too.

Nothing is sent to the server: everything is measured client-side.
cfc_search.tip.search:
Search
Outlines matching components and dims the others. Enter / Shift+Enter = next / previous, Ctrl+F = focus, right-click = clear.
text: item name
@mod: item's mod (@create)
#tag: item tag (#c:ingots)
$text: in the tooltip
>address: delivery address (>PRESS)
-word: exclude
cfc_search.tip.stats_button:
Stats
Shows the speed of each delivery address, the CSV/Excel export and the AI analysis.
cfc_search.tip.col.address:
Address
The delivery address set in the gauges (the Frogport / machine receiving the packages). All gauges sending to the same address are grouped.
cfc_search.tip.col.status:
Status
The worst situation among this address's gauges. Hover a cell for details.
cfc_search.tip.col.waiting:
Waiting
Waiting gauges / gauges of this address. "Waiting" = below target and not stopped by redstone.
cfc_search.tip.col.max:
Longest wait
How long the oldest gauge has been waiting. Past 3 min with a package on its way, the address turns "slow".
cfc_search.tip.col.rate:
Rate per minute
Items that actually reached the stock per minute (observed stock increases). "…" = not measured long enough yet (keep the screen open a few seconds).
cfc_search.tip.status.slow:
SLOW
A package left more than 3 min ago and nothing came back. Either the machine is too slow or the package never arrives: check the address spelling on the Frogport, heating (blaze burner), a full or stuck Frogport. The Excel report tells the two apart.
cfc_search.tip.status.missing:
MISSING INGREDIENTS
The gauge wants to send an order but ingredients are missing from the network. The problem is upstream: look at which gauge makes the ingredient (Chain sheet of the report).
cfc_search.tip.status.waiting:
WAITING
Some gauges are below target, but for less than 3 min or with no package on its way. Normal while running, worrying if it lasts.
cfc_search.tip.status.ok:
OK
Every gauge of this address has reached its target.
cfc_search.tip.footer:
Measurement
Stats are only taken while this screen is open (the client can't see the factory otherwise). Click a line = search >address.
cfc_search.tip.csv:
CSV recording + report
One snapshot every 10 s for the chosen duration, as long as this screen stays open. At the end: two CSVs (gauges, families) and an Excel report with charts and prioritised actions.
Tip: at least 15-20 min for a reliable diagnosis.
cfc_search.tip.csv_stop:
Stop
Ends the recording now and writes the report from what was measured.
cfc_search.tip.open_folder:
Open folder
Opens the export folder (CSVs, Excel reports, texts sent to the AI) and shows its path in chat (click = copy).
Default: cfc_search_exports in the game folder. Change it with export_dir in config/cfc_search.properties.
cfc_search.tip.ai:
Analyse with AI
Copies every piece of data about this controller to the clipboard (last finished recording, otherwise an instant snapshot) and opens the AI site (claude.ai by default). Paste with Ctrl+V.
For a better analysis: also attach the Excel report (*_report.xlsx) and the two CSVs of the last recording, found in the export folder ("Open folder" button). The AI gets the full second-by-second history from them.
The site opened is set in config/cfc_search.properties (ai_url).
cfc_search.tip.book:
Address book
Left-click a line = fills the gauge's address field. "Copy" button (on hover) or right-click = copies the full address to paste with Ctrl+V on the Frogport.
In green: the processing types able to make this item (detected through JEI). Below: your categories, editable in config/cfc_search-adresses.json.
Tip: one address per machine type (e.g. processing/pressing) makes the report much easier to read.
cfc_search.tip.book_suggested:
Suggested for this item
The recipes making the gauge's item, with the matching processing address. If there are several, pick the machine you actually built.
cfc_search.tip.network:
Network
Default: none, addresses stay processing/smelting. Pick a network so book addresses become network/type/name (e.g. mine/processing/smelting), useful when several logistics networks each have their own machines.
Left-click = next network, right-click = previous. The choice is remembered for this Factory Controller.
Remember to put the same address on the machine's Frogport.
cfc_search.tip.stats_network:
Network filter
This controller sends to several networks (prefix/type/name addresses). Click = next network, then "all". When filtered, addresses are shown without the prefix.
cfc_search.help.col.network: Network prefix of the address (prefix/type/name). "default" = address without prefix.
cfc_search.help.text.networks: A three-part address prefix/type/name (e.g. mine/processing/smelting) belongs to network "mine". A one- or two-part address (processing/smelting, PRESS A) belongs to the default network. The prefix is set in each gauge's address book and remembered per Factory Controller. The report adds a Network column and, when there are several, a per-network table in Overview. The same address in two networks is not flagged as a typo.
cfc_search.tip.network_add:
New network
Type a name then Enter (or click + again). Escape = cancel. The network is created and selected for this controller.
cfc_search.tip.network_remove:
Forget this network
Removes it from the list and from the controllers using it (back to "none"). Addresses already written in gauges don't change.
cfc_search.tip.book_copy:
Copy address
Puts the full address (with the network) in the clipboard, to paste with Ctrl+V on the machine's Frogport. Right-click a line = same.
